correctness.rationale: The spherical three-point plane coarea separates plane height density f_H(h)=3(1-h²)/2 from angular area-weighted triangle law. Independently evaluated J0=3π/8 and JA=3π/16 by two-dimensional high-precision quadrature, so the limiting acute fraction is one-half and normalized mark density 16/(3π). When face height h→0, the cone of its vertices contains the origin with a random independent fourth vertex exactly in the limiting acute projected-triangle/negative-hemisphere event; the latter has conditional probability one-half. Thus each marked face contributes (3/2)(1/2)(1/2)=3/8 to first-order mass. For two different faces, the second face height remains positive a.s. at generic first-face h=0, giving overlapping event mass o(t) via dominated convergence; the four contributions sum to 3/2. Wendel’s symmetric-point formula gives Pr(E)=1/8. Four caps cover iff B_t(0)⊆conv(X1..X4), producing the p expansion. Rescaling h=ts and dominated convergence/Scheffé control densities in total variation; overlaps o(t) give a single nearest-face mark. Independently sampled 150000 triples and checked the exact plane-height CDF at thresholds .05 and .1; this diagnoses but cannot prove the small-t limit or TV assertion.
